1 Scientific Literature.Title: Study on the Carbonation Behavior of Steel Slag in the SiC-K2SiO3 System Assisted by Microwave Heating
1 Scientific Literature.Authors: Wei Long, Wenxiao Fu, Wenming Jiang
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Accelerate carbonation of BOF steel slag compacts by coupling microwave heating, SiC absorber and potassium silicate activation.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: At L/S 0.14 and 90 °C microwave for 45 min, compressive strength peaked at 48.82 MPa (+44.7% vs conventional) with CO2 uptake ~16.4%; average pore size reduced to 43 nm. 60 min heating caused thermal damage and strength loss. Calcite grows within a K-silicate gel network.

2 Feedstock Chemistry.Source/Origin: BOF steel slag powder, China Baowu Steel Group (Shanghai)
2 Feedstock Chemistry.Notes: Table 1; others 1.21. Phases: brownmillerite, portlandite, larnite, donathite, wüstite, srebrodolskite. Density 3.541 g/cm3.

3 Processing.Equipment_or_Process: Vacuum oven 60 °C 24 h; press forming 120 s; microwave reactor FCMCR-3SX
3 Processing.Processing_Notes: Vacuum-oven drying 60 °C 24 h; compacts then carbonated with microwave heating at 70-90 °C (sheets 5, 6 and 8)
